title: ℤ[X,Y] and Multivariate Polynomial Rings are UFDs
description: Proves that ℤ[X,Y] is a unique factorization domain, extending the parent proof (UFD for R[X] when R is a UFD) to multivariate polynomial rings. The key results are: (1) ℤ[X][Y] = Polynomial(Polynomial ℤ) is a UFD via two applications of Gauss's lemma, (2) MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ is a UFD for any n, (3) MvPolynomial σ R is a UFD for any fintype σ and UFD R. Irreducibility and Euclid's lemma extend to the multivariate setting.

overview.historicalContext: Gauss's *Disquisitiones Arithmeticae* (1801) established unique factorization in ℤ and his lemma — that a primitive polynomial in ℤ[X] is irreducible over ℤ iff irreducible over ℚ — implies ℤ[X] is a UFD. The abstract generalization 'if R is a UFD then R[X] is a UFD' was placed on rigorous footing in Emmy Noether's foundational papers on ideal theory (1921-1926), which gave the axiomatic framework now used in commutative algebra. By induction, R[X₁,...,Xₙ] is a UFD for any UFD R and finite n; Kronecker (1882) had argued this via his divisor theory. Hilbert's Basis Theorem (1888) ensures that polynomial rings over Noetherian rings are Noetherian, making ℤ[X,Y] the canonical example of a Noetherian UFD that is *not* a PID — the ideal (2, X) in ℤ[X] is not principal, a fact that distinguishes polynomial rings from rings of integers. In algebraic geometry, ℤ[X,Y] is the coordinate ring of the affine plane $\mathbb{A}^2_{\mathbb{Z}}$; the UFD property ensures algebraic varieties defined by irreducible polynomials decompose uniquely into irreducible components. Zariski and Samuel's *Commutative Algebra* (Vol. I, 1958) gave the definitive modern treatment. Mathlib formalizes the full abstract hierarchy (UFD, GCD domain, PID, Noetherian) and provides MvPolynomial.uniqueFactorizationMonoid as a typeclass instance.
overview.problemStatement: Is ℤ[X,Y] a UFD? More generally, is MvPolynomial σ ℤ a UFD for finite σ?
overview.text: ℤ[X,Y] and more generally MvPolynomial σ R (for UFD R and fintype σ) are UFDs.
overview.proofStrategy: Apply Gauss's lemma (Polynomial.uniqueFactorizationMonoid) iteratively: ℤ → ℤ[X] → (ℤ[X])[Y]. For MvPolynomial, Mathlib provides the instance directly via MvPolynomial.uniqueFactorizationMonoid. Irreducibility of variables follows from MvPolynomial.X_prime and irreducible_iff_prime.
keyInsights: Gauss's lemma: UFD R → UFD R[X] generalizes to all finite variable counts
MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ ≃ₐ Polynomial (Polynomial ℤ) — the two representations are isomorphic
Every variable Xᵢ is prime (and hence irreducible) in MvPolynomial σ R
The UFD structure relies on finiteness of the variable set σ — infinitely many variables break UFD

The distinction between UFD and PID is sharp for polynomial rings: ℤ[X] is a UFD but not a PID (the ideal (2, X) requires two generators), and ℤ[X,Y] is further from being a PID. The Noetherian property (every ideal is finitely generated) holds for all polynomial rings over Noetherian rings by Hilbert's Basis Theorem, but being a PID requires every ideal to be *principal* — a much stronger condition that polynomial rings in ≥1 variable fail even over fields (e.g., ℚ[X,Y] is a UFD but not a PID). This places ℤ[X,Y] in the hierarchy: Euclidean domain ⊂ PID ⊂ UFD ⊂ GCD domain ⊂ integral domain, and ℤ[X,Y] occupies precisely the UFD level.

sections.title: Iterated Univariate: ℤ[X][Y] is a UFD
sections.summary: UFD chain: ℤ → ℤ[X] → (ℤ[X])[Y] via Gauss's lemma.
sections.mathContext: Gauss's lemma chain: $\mathbb{Z}$ (UFD) $\Rightarrow$ $\text{Polynomial}\,\mathbb{Z}$ (UFD) $\Rightarrow$ $\text{Polynomial}\,(\text{Polynomial}\,\mathbb{Z})$ (UFD). Each step by \texttt{Polynomial.uniqueFactorizationMonoid}: if $[\text{UniqueFactorizationMonoid}\,R]$ then $\text{UniqueFactorizationMonoid}\,(R[X])$. The iterated ring $\mathbb{Z}[X][Y] \cong \mathbb{Z}[X,Y]$ as an abstract ring.

sections.title: Multivariate Polynomial Rings
sections.summary: MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ is a UFD; general statement for any UFD R and fintype σ.
sections.mathContext: $\text{MvPolynomial}\,(\text{Fin}\,2)\,\mathbb{Z}$ (i.e., $\mathbb{Z}[X,Y]$) is a UFD: \texttt{MvPolynomial.uniqueFactorizationMonoid} with $[\text{Fintype}\,\sigma]$, $[\text{UniqueFactorizationMonoid}\,R]$. General: for any UFD $R$ and fintype $\sigma$, $\text{MvPolynomial}\,\sigma\,R$ is a UFD. Special cases: $\mathbb{Q}[X,Y]$ (field case), $k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ for any field $k$.

sections.title: Irreducible = Prime in ℤ[X,Y]
sections.summary: Irreducible ↔ prime; Euclid's lemma for ℤ[X,Y].
sections.mathContext: In a UFD: $p$ irreducible $\Leftrightarrow$ $p$ prime ($p \mid ab \Rightarrow p \mid a$ or $p \mid b$). Proved via \texttt{UniqueFactorizationMonoid.irreducible\_iff\_prime}. Euclid's lemma: $p$ irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[X,Y]$ and $p \mid fg$ implies $p \mid f$ or $p \mid g$. This is the polynomial analog of Euclid's lemma for $\mathbb{Z}$.

sections.title: Irreducible Elements
sections.summary: Variables X, Y are irreducible; general xi_irred_in_mv_poly.
sections.mathContext: $X = \text{MvPolynomial.X}\,0$ and $Y = \text{MvPolynomial.X}\,1$ are prime in $\mathbb{Z}[X,Y]$ (\texttt{MvPolynomial.X\_prime}) and hence irreducible (by \texttt{irreducible\_iff\_prime}). General: for any $i : \sigma$, $X_i \in \text{MvPolynomial}\,\sigma\,R$ is irreducible when $R$ is a UFD. The ideal $(X_i)$ is prime in $\text{MvPolynomial}\,\sigma\,R$.

conclusion.summary: Complete proof that ℤ[X,Y] and general multivariate polynomial rings over UFDs are UFDs, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Provides the foundation for algebraic geometry: polynomial rings over ℤ or fields are the canonical UFDs used as coordinate rings.
openQuestions: Can we prove ℤ[X,Y] is NOT a PID? (It's not: (2, X) is not principal.)
Can we formalize the Nullstellensatz in this multivariate UFD context?
